Context: the repo's ADR corpus (52 files in `decisions/`) was audited today against the three ADR hurdles from Matt Pocock's domain-modeling skill. The finding: most files bundle 5 to 15 numbered items (D1..D15), and most items are spec restatement, test duties, accepted residuals, or "the old bug" listed as a rejected alternative. The owner wants the process text to enforce the bar per item from now on.

Rewrite "### ADR Process" in AGENTS.md so that it states, in this order and in short paragraphs or a short list:
1. The existing mechanics, kept verbatim in meaning: an ADR is a `docs:` PR that adds one file to `decisions/` with status Proposed; open as draft with `@coderabbitai ignore` in the body; the owner accepts by merging with the status changed to "Accepted on <date>"; a blueprint or `CONTEXT.md` reword the Consequences list goes in the same PR or the next one; an ADR that amends an older ADR adds one "Amended by ADR 00NN Dk on <date>: …" sentence at the amended item in the older file, in the same PR.
2. The bar. Every decision item must pass all three hurdles, and an ADR that has no item that passes all three is not written: (1) hard to reverse — the cost of a later change is meaningful: a wire format, a KDF edge, a trust boundary, a durable storage shape, a protocol, a term the corpus uses; (2) surprising without context — a reader of the code would ask why; (3) the result of a real trade-off — genuine alternatives existed and one was picked for stated reasons. State the three named non-decisions: the bug before a fix is not an alternative; a test duty, an accepted residual, a deferral, a schedule, a numeric default or a "nothing changes" note is not a decision — it goes in Consequences or in the blueprint, in one line.
3. Shape. One decision per ADR; a second decision is a second ADR or an "Amended by" sentence. Sections: the header list (Status, Date, Relates to, Implemented by, Amends), Context (the reason, at most a short paragraph), Decision (the items, numbered D1.. so they can be cited), Alternatives considered (real options only), Consequences (one line per document that changes), Residuals (open owner questions only). No Gate section: the tests that prove an ADR are named in `blueprint/testing.md`, not in the ADR. No file-and-line citations; cite a module, a function or a blueprint section. Target under 120 lines.
4. Retroactive ADRs (written after the code shipped) meet the same bar; "the blueprint already carries it" is a reason to cite the blueprint, not to write an item.
5. Trim rule for existing files: when an item is removed from an accepted ADR, its number is not reused, and one line "Items Dx and Dy moved to `blueprint/<file>.md` "<section>" on <date>" replaces it, so citations like `ADR 0033 D2` still resolve.

Keep the subsection under 40 lines. Then update the README intro above the table so it states the same bar in at most 4 sentences and points to AGENTS.md "ADR Process" for the full text (keep its existing sentences about file naming, status, "Amended by", and the archived cipher-box-next repo).

Run `pnpm exec prettier --write AGENTS.md decisions/README.md` and `pnpm exec markdownlint AGENTS.md decisions/README.md` and fix what they report (MD036 no bold-as-heading; MD031/MD032 blank lines around fences and lists). Check with `git diff --stat` that only those two files changed by you (other agents' files may also show; ignore them).

Prose rules for both files and for your report: ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English — short sentences (under 25 words), active voice, simple present or past, no -ing verb forms, no contractions, no idioms, one term per thing. Code, identifiers and quoted text are exempt. No tool attribution. Do not add tracker references in the form `#1234`.

Report (under 200 words): the new subsection text verbatim, and the README sentences you changed.

questions.question: Eight items inside Accepted ADRs say "for the owner to accept": 0041 D1 (a root-arm publish re-reads the cut-epoch floor too), 0042 D8 (a re-author keeps every critical field), 0043 D5 (every soft delete re-keys the subtree), 0043 D9 (restore re-keys, relinks, then drops the entry), 0044 D3 (the poll tick has no jitter), 0044 D8 (a host that cannot measure headroom is unmeasurable, not full), 0045 D5 (the overlay stamps mtime from authored_at), 0045 D6 (a move is one entry, one kernel rename). All eight describe what the code does today. How do you rule?

options.label: Accept all eight (Recommended)
options.description: Pro: the ADRs match the code and the sentence "for the owner to accept" goes away. Con: 0044 D3 is code-local and a later change needs a new ADR or an amendment.

options.label: Accept all but some
options.description: Write the exceptions in Other. The rest are accepted, the exceptions stay marked Proposed inside the file.

options.label: Mark all eight Proposed
options.description: Pro: no ruling under time pressure. Con: eight Accepted files carry Proposed items until a later pass.

questions.question: ADR 0029 E1: the code lags D1. Every record head block still goes to the hosted ingress in every mode, so an account that picks External placement gets a 409 on its first file write and can never publish. Which way?

options.label: Keep D1, fix the code (Recommended)
options.description: Pro: the decision stands, the record head block follows placement. Con: an engine fix must land before External placement is usable; I file one issue for it.

options.label: Change D1 to match the code
options.description: The hosted leg always carries the record head block, in every mode. Pro: no engine work. Con: a BYO account still depends on the hosted store for every record.

options.label: Leave E1 open
options.description: No ruling now. The ADR keeps the residual as an open owner question.

questions.question: ADR 0031 E4: the genesis publish raises the durable mint counter before the PUT, so one failed first publish strands that device for good. Recovery today is a hard delete or a second device. Which way?

options.label: Accept as a defect, fix it (Recommended)
options.description: Pro: the strand goes away; the counter should mark only a PUT that can have landed. Con: an engine fix in the bin index genesis path; I file one issue for it.

options.label: Accept the strand as a residual
options.description: Pro: no engine work. Con: a failed first PUT on a device is permanent for that device, and the ADR records that as accepted.

options.label: Leave E4 open
options.description: No ruling now.

questions.question: ADR 0039 E1: D4 says desktop is a device-approval requester only, but no rendezvous role exists on desktop at all, and the cutover closed without it. Issue 2010 tracks the requester leg. Which way?

options.label: Keep D4, 2010 stays the residual (Recommended)
options.description: Pro: the product rule stands and the open issue carries the work. Con: the ADR describes a role the code does not have until 2010 lands.

options.label: Rule that as-built is the decision
options.description: No rendezvous role on desktop. Pro: the ADR matches the code today. Con: D4, one alternative, one consequence and one blueprint bullet get reworded, and 2010 closes as not planned.

resolution of FSM1/cipher-box#830, a map FSM1/cipher-box#813 ticket.

The blueprint states a different set today: "Every op but a delete authors its target's next
record, so the overlay stamps `mtime = authored_at`" (`blueprint/engine.md` "Sync core", the
state-law bullet). That target-only form first appeared in the body of FSM1/cipher-box#878,
which an agent wrote, and no owner decision stands behind it. It contradicts the resolution of
FSM1/cipher-box#830. This ADR proposes the FSM1/cipher-box#830 set as the rule, for the owner
to accept. The code does not meet it yet (E3).

**D6 — A `move` is a relink and a rename in one entry, and one kernel rename is one
command.** The intent op list of `#33` D5 gains `move`. A `move` carries the relink, the rename
and, optionally, the node already at the destination name that it vacates. At rebase, the move
vacates the destination node only while that node still holds the contested name. One kernel
rename is one command. A relocation between two interior scopes journals as a parking leg and
an arriving leg, and both legs are journaled or neither is. The parking leg is a `relink` out of
the source scope into the vault-root scope; it leaves the granted source, so it carries the cut
that the whole relocation owes. The arriving leg is the op the caller asked for, from the vault
root into the destination scope, and it re-seals the subtree and cuts nothing. Every other
relocation journals as one entry. A replace is never observable half-done.

The single `move` landed with FSM1/cipher-box#897. The two-leg plan landed with
FSM1/cipher-box#1765, which an agent wrote and which says that no blueprint sentence changes.
No owner decision exists for either. The blueprint says "one POSIX rename is exactly one
`move`" (`blueprint/engine.md` "Ops") and "exactly one facade intent op" (`blueprint/desktop.md`

accepts the rule above with this ADR.

vacates the destination node only while that node still holds the contested name. One kernel

the source scope into the vault-root scope; it leaves the granted source, so it carries the cut

each pass and wakes early only on a manual refresh. The production cadence is 30 s. The

term and takes no entropy. No owner decision exists for this rule. The rule landed with

cat > /tmp/issue-0031-e4.md <<'EOF'
## Problem

`publish_bin_index` in `crates/engine/src/bin_index.rs` raises the durable mint counter before it draws the nonce, seals, preflights and runs the PUT. A publish that fails after the raise, for any reason, leaves the mint counter as the only mark on the device. `holds_a_bin_index_mark` then reads the mark, and every later genesis attempt on that device stops before it sends a request. `unresolved_reason` gives `StrandedMint`, and `halt_for_bin_load` dead-letters every soft delete on that device. Nothing on the device clears the mark.

The genesis publish runs on every first run, so one failed PUT at vault genesis strands the device for good. The only recovery today is a hard delete or a second device.

ADR 0031 residual E4 records this. The owner ruled on 2026-09-26 that this is a defect, not an accepted residual.

## Fix

The mint counter must mark only a PUT that can have landed. Raise the counter after the request leaves the engine, or record the attempt in a form that a later genesis attempt can retry. A failure before the request leaves the engine must leave no mark. A failure after it leaves the engine keeps the mark, because the PUT can have landed.

Add a test that fails the genesis publish before the request and shows that the next attempt publishes.

## Where

- `crates/engine/src/bin_index.rs` (`publish_bin_index`, `holds_a_bin_index_mark`)
- `crates/engine/src/record_plane.rs` (`unresolved_reason`)
- `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs` (`halt_for_bin_load`)
- ADR 0031 E4 and `blueprint/engine.md` "Bin index record" carry the rule after the fix.
EOF
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh issue create --repo FSM1/cipher-box --title "fix(engine): the bin index genesis mint mark must not strand a device after a failed first PUT" --label v2-build --label comp:engine --body-file /tmp/issue-0031-e4.md 2>&1 | tail -1

## Decision

1. **The PR gate is grouped by area.** `ci.yml` is one caller that holds the path filters and
   calls one reusable workflow per area: Repo, API, Rust, Web, Desktop. A job's name states what
   it checks and in which language. Each TypeScript package is typechecked, tested, and built once,
   inside its area.
2. **Each area ends in one stable result context.** The result job needs every job of its area,
   runs always, fails when any needed job failed or was cancelled, and passes when every needed
   job succeeded or was skipped by the path filter. Branch protection requires the result contexts
   and the standalone contexts that stay outside an area. It requires no job inside an area.
3. **The PR gate has an adapter leg per shipped desktop platform.** The macOS and Windows legs
   each run a workspace check with all targets, the tests of the OS adapter crates, and the
   keyring conformance suite against the real OS backend. Neither leg runs the engine simulation:
   the engine is platform-neutral and the Linux Rust area owns it. Linux adapter coverage stays
   on the main-gate mounted matrix, where a mount exists.
